statement: conformal ALD in macroscopic nanoporous solids with AR above 10^3 may need reactant exposures of about 10^3 Torr-s or more
with some ALD chemistries, exposures that large make non-self-limiting growth a concern
DEZ/H2O ZnO ALD with exposures between 10 and 10^3 Torr-s has given metallic Zn at temperatures usual for wafers, e.g. ~180 °C
a lower deposition temperature suppresses the Zn deposition but slows H2O desorption, which can force impractically long purges
the static-dose DEZ and H2O exposures used here exceed 10^4 Torr-s
the temperature-cycled process gives apparently self-limiting ZnO growth with a conductive ZnO network uniform through the NPC thickness, apart from some ZnO depletion near the faces
the T = 120 °C process gives results like the cycled one but with a slightly higher GPC, pointing to less H2O and/or OH removed during purges
the three processes are compared with SEM-EDS, XRD, electrical resistivity and analysis of the ALD chamber pressure
ALD can coat the inner surfaces of porous nanoparticle networks and so change their optical, electronic or structural properties
self-limiting half-reactions can in principle coat the whole inner surface of an NP network uniformly if the pores are open and the whole surface sees enough reactant
aspect ratio AR of an NP network: its thickness L divided by the mean pore diameter d_pore
the minimum exposure needed depends on the network porosity φ and on the AR
for NP thin films with porosity ~0.3 to ~0.5 and AR ~100 or less (L ~100 nm to ~1 µm, d_pore ~5 to ~20 nm) about 1 Torr or less of reactant suffices
for such NP thin films an exposure time of about 1 s or less is usually enough
NP thin films have been ALD-coated with Al2O3, HfO2 and ZnO
a ZnO coating is attractive for its semiconducting behaviour and because it enables bandlike transport in NP networks
scaling the substrate up from NP thin films to mm-scale NP networks with L of order 1 mm and AR of order 10^4 could widen applications but needs much larger exposures

using a lower temperature to avoid Zn is hard to apply to conductive ZnO coatings on macroscopic NP networks for two reasons
below ~170 °C the resistivity of ALD ZnO often rises with deposition temperature, through the temperature dependence of stoichiometry, grain size and orientation

the process designs follow theory by Yanguas-Gil and Elam and the study of Cendejas et al. on exposure and purge times for uniform coating of nanostructures
Eq. (1): hold time t_hold = L_pore^2 / (D γ); used to set the hold times
L_pore: mean pore length including tortuosity

θ_f: the fractional coverage of adsorbed H2O left after the purge

E_des, the H2O desorption energy, is taken as independent of coverage
